title: Epimorphic covers of successor boundaries by incoming cycle representatives
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $K$ an integer-indexed cochain complex and $F$ a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. Let $r\ge1$ and $i,j\in\mathbb Z^2$ satisfy $i+(r,1-r)=j$. Use the graded cycles and boundaries of [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients], writing $n_i=i_1+i_2$ and $n_j=j_1+j_2$ and $\pi_p:F^pK^n\to\operatorname{gr}^pK^n$. There exist an object $A$, an epimorphism $e:A\to B_{r+1}^{j_1,n_j}$, maps $t:A\to F^{i_1}K^{n_i}$ and $t\prime:A\to F^{j_1}K^{n_j}$, and $x:A\to Z_r^{i_1,n_i}$ such that $t\,\iota_{i_1}\,d=t\prime\,\iota_{j_1}$, $x\,\iota_{Z_r}=t\,\pi_{i_1}$, and $e\,\iota_{B_{r+1}\to Z_{r+1}}\,\iota_{Z_{r+1}}=t\prime\,\pi_{j_1}$, where the boundary-to-cycle inclusion is [lem-sp-filtered-complex-boundaries-le-cycles]. This assertion is independent of any page differential or homology object.

proof.text: Let j=(p,q), n=p+q. The relation gives i=(p-r,q+r-1) and incoming degree n-1. Let U=F^p K^n intersect image(d restricted to F^(p-r) K^(n-1)), and V its pullback to F^p K^n. Since U and F^(p+1) lie in F^p, pulling back their sum is the sum of their pullbacks. Image pushforward preserves this sum. The graded projection kills F^(p+1), so image(V -> gr^p K^n) equals B_(r+1). Use the image factorization to obtain an epimorphism e0:V -> B_(r+1).

source.place: Tag 012K, displayed boundary and differential formulas before lemma-spectral-sequence-filtered-complex

proof.text: The map V -> K^n factors through the image of d restricted to F^(p-r) K^(n-1), by the right-hand intersection inclusion. Refine this map along the epimorphic factor of the differential image factorization. Mathlib surjective_up_to_refinements_of_epi gives an object A, an epimorphism e1:A -> V, and t:A -> F^(p-r) K^(n-1) whose differential equals tprime=e1 followed by V -> F^p K^n. The composite e=e1 e0 is epic.

proof.text: Because dt=tprime lies in F^p, the map t factors through the incoming r-cycle representative subobject. Include it into the sum with F^(p-r+1) used to define graded cycles, and use the image factorization of the graded projection to obtain x:A -> Z_r at i. This gives the source representative equation.

proof.text: The factorization defining e0 gives e followed by the boundary arrow equal to tprime followed by the graded projection. The successor-boundary inclusion followed by the successor-cycle arrow is the boundary arrow. This gives the target representative equation.

theorem filteredComplex_successor_boundary_representatives
    (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (F : DecreasingFiltration K) (r : ℤ) (_hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (i j : ℤ × ℤ) (hij : (ComplexShape.up' (r, 1 - r)).Rel i j) :
    ∃ (A : C) (e : A ⟶ (F.complexBoundaries j.1 (j.1 + j.2) (r + 1) : C)),
      Epi e ∧
      ∃ (t : A ⟶ (F.step i.1 : CochainComplex C ℤ).X (i.1 + i.2))
        (t' : A ⟶ (F.step j.1 : CochainComplex C ℤ).X (j.1 + j.2))
        (x : A ⟶ (F.complexCycles i.1 (i.1 + i.2) r : C)),
        t ≫ (F.step i.1).arrow.f (i.1 + i.2) ≫ K.d (i.1 + i.2) (j.1 + j.2) =
          t' ≫ (F.step j.1).arrow.f (j.1 + j.2) ∧
        x ≫ (F.complexCycles i.1 (i.1 + i.2) r).arrow =
          t ≫ (F.complexQuotientπ i.1 (i.1 + 1) (by omega)).f (i.1 + i.2) ∧
        e ≫ Subobject.ofLE _ _
            (filteredComplex_boundaries_le_cycles K F j.1 (j.1 + j.2) (r + 1)) ≫
            (F.complexCycles j.1 (j.1 + j.2) (r + 1)).arrow =
          t' ≫ (F.complexQuotientπ j.1 (j.1 + 1) (by omega)).f (j.1 + j.2)
